topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer treatment modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene Targeting and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapies directed against oncogenic driver mutations and hyperactive kinases, detailing their molecular mechanisms, resistance pathways, and dosing strategies.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates target specific cell-surface antigens to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Modulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the principles and applications of cancer immunotherapy, focusing on immune surveillance, checkpoint blockade, and engineered T-cell technologies.

topics.label: Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overarching challenges in cancer management, historical trends in patient survival, and emerging directions in clinical translation and ethics.
